question: Will a Préfecture de Police curfew be in effect anywhere in Paris on the night of New Year's Eve 2026?

calls.reasoning: Base rate of a Paris Préfecture de Police NYE curfew in non-COVID years is ~0. But in Oct 2026 the Préfecture repeatedly issued night curfews (all-persons around République/Les Halles 23:00-06:00 Oct 19 onward and again Oct 31-Nov 2; minors-only 21:00-06:00 Oct 30-Nov 2), including event-targeted ones for Halloween. Curfews ended Nov 2; movement is de-escalating (turnout -40% from peak, concessions Oct 26) though the Nov 5 strike was large with incidents. One minors curfew was suspended by the Paris administrative court on Oct 28. NYE is a recognized unrest night; a targeted minors or perimeter curfew is plausible if unrest persists into December. Estimate: P(unrest still significant late Dec) ~0.3 x P(curfew|unrest) ~0.5 + P(curfew|calm) ~0.05. No human market found for this contract (Polymarket only had a curfew-lifting market and a state-of-emergency market).
calls.dossier:
- Event window: 23:00 Dec 31, 2026 -> 06:00 Jan 1, 2027 (curfew must be in effect then in any part of the City of Paris, per a Préfecture de Police order). As of Nov 5, 2026, 0% of the window has elapsed; it starts in ~8 weeks.
- Resolves off a Préfecture de Police arrêté (arrêtés page) or credible reports. The criterion does not specify all-persons, so a minors-only curfew order arguably counts.
- Background (NPR/WaPo, Oct 20-21, 2026): after the Oct 17-18 riots, France announced nightly curfews 'for as long as necessary' in Paris, Lyon, Bordeaux, Nice, Lille and other cities. The Paris curfew was 23:00-06:00 around Place de la République and Châtelet-Les Halles from Oct 19-20. More than 2,500 arrests nationally.
- Paris administrative court (Oct 28, 2026) suspended a minors' curfew (21:00-06:00, Mon-Thu Oct 26-29) after a challenge by the association Vigie Liberté. The court found the prefecture had not shown specific risks involving minors (titrespresse/fdesouche).
- Préfecture re-issued orders right away (laclepublique, Oct 30): arrêté 2026-01478 imposed a minors' curfew 21:00-06:00 for Oct 30-Nov 2 across many sectors in arrondissements 1,4,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,13,15,17. It cited 130 minors among 557 people in custody on Oct 17-18. Arrêté 2026-01485 imposed an all-persons curfew 23:00-06:00 for Oct 31-Nov 2 in the République/Les Halles perimeters, citing the expected Halloween-weekend mobilization. This shows the Préfecture is willing to issue curfews targeted at specific event nights.
- Current status (parisjetaime/samanthatravels, early Nov): no curfew in Paris since 06:00 Nov 2.
- Trajectory (samanthatravels timeline): national turnout ~500k on Oct 17, ~410k on Oct 24, ~320k on Oct 31. Government concessions on Oct 26 (Parcoursup replacement, class caps, €4bn for schools).
- Nov 5, 2026 general strike (franceinfo/France24): very strong participation in Paris; hooded vandals at the head of the march; projectiles thrown; a car burned. Intelligence services classed the day 'at risk'; 70,000 police and gendarmes deployed.
- PM Lecornu credited the curfews with bringing calm (ABC). Polymarket and Kalshi have related markets on state of emergency and curfew lifting, but none on a NYE curfew.
- Historical: Paris NYE normally sees heavy policing, fireworks-sales bans and car burnings in the suburbs (riots at end of 2025 per question background). Apart from the 2020 COVID-era national curfew, no known Préfecture curfew on NYE.
- Countervailing: NYE features mass celebrations (Champs-Élysées), and a general curfew conflicts with them. Courts have pushed back on minors' curfews.
- Searched but not found: any announced NYE 2026 security plan or curfew; any human market on this exact contract; protest calendar for December 2026.
calls.reference_class: Paris NYE nights (non-COVID) with a Préfecture de Police curfew order; plus event-targeted curfews during the active phase of the 2026 unrest

calls.reasoning: Base rate of a Paris city-proper curfew on NYE in normal years is ~1-3% (none in 2005, 2023 or 2025 unrest). But autumn 2026 the Préfecture issued repeated event-targeted curfews (Oct 19 onward République/Halles 23h-6h; reinstated for Oct 31-Nov 2 Halloween/march weekend; minors' curfews Oct 26-29 (suspended by court) and Oct 30-Nov 2). As of Nov 5 no curfew in effect, movement de-escalating (marches 550k->410k->320k, government concessions Oct 26), courts skeptical of minors' curfews, ~8 weeks to NYE through Christmas holidays. NYE is a known flashpoint and the prefecture now has a template for one-off event-night curfews, so meaningful but minority probability. Market: no matching market; Polymarket 'Paris curfew lifted by' (~$64k) priced ~97% lifted by Nov 30 — near-miss, evidence only.
calls.dossier:
- Sept 2026: high-school/university protests over school conditions; Oct 17 ~550k march nationwide, looting at République/Les Halles, cars burned in 10th arr. (samanthatravels timeline; NPR 2026-10-21).
- Oct 19-21: Préfecture de Police imposes 23:00-06:00 curfew around Place de la République and Châtelet-Les Halles; govt said curfews 'for as long as necessary' (NPR, WaPo 2026-10-20). >2,500 arrests.
- Oct 24 march ~410k; Oct 26 govt concessions (class caps, €4bn renovation, Parcoursup replacement).
- Oct 26-29 minors' curfew suspended by Paris Administrative Court Oct 28 as 'serious infringement of freedom of movement' (sortiraparis).
- Oct 30: Arrêté 2026-01485 reinstated République/Halles curfew for nights Oct 31-Nov 1 and Nov 1-2 (ended 06:00 Nov 2); new minors' curfew 21:00-06:00 Oct 30-Nov 2 in several sectors (economiematin; sortiraparis).
- Oct 31 march ~320k; Molotov hit gendarme; >770 arrests.
- As of ~Nov 3-5: no curfew in effect in Paris (parisjetaime/travel sites). Nov 5 national strike, 70,000 police nationwide, 25 metro stations closed, route République->Nation imposed by prefecture (cnews 2026-11-04).
- Pattern: curfews issued as short, event-targeted arrêtés with ~1-2 days notice around big protest weekends/Halloween.
- Historical: no Paris city-proper curfew on NYE in 2005 (riots), 2023 (Nahel riots aftermath), or 2025 (NYE riots in suburbs); usual NYE measures are firework sale bans, gathering bans, heavy policing. ~1M at Champs-Elysées NYE 2025-26.
- No announced protest dates beyond Nov 5 found; no reporting on NYE 2026 security plans found.
- Market: no NYE-specific market found on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmakers; a Polymarket 'Paris curfew lifted by' market exists (different contract).
- Resolution: resolves off Préfecture de Police arrêtés page or credible reports; any curfew (incl. minors-only arguably) in any part of City of Paris (not suburbs/other prefects).
- Event window: 23:00 Dec 31 2026 -> 06:00 Jan 1 2027 per the criteria; as of 2026-11-05, 0% elapsed (~56 days before window).
calls.reference_class: Paris New Year's Eves (city proper) with any prefectoral curfew, incl. years following major unrest (2005, 2023, 2025)

calls.reasoning: Status quo: no curfew. The Paris curfews (République/Les Halles 23:00-06:00, plus a 21:00 curfew for unaccompanied minors in several zones) ended at 06:00 on Nov 2, 2026. Base rate: the Préfecture de Police has essentially never imposed a curfew on New Year's Eve outside COVID (2020). Its normal NYE tools are bans on fireworks, fuel and alcohol sales. Pushing the other way: during this unrest the Préfecture has shown it will use curfews readily and bring them back for specific risky nights, as it did for the Halloween weekend. A minors-only curfew in some zones would probably count under 'any part'. NYE also has a history of car-burning. Pushing down: weekly turnout has fallen each Saturday (550k, then 410k, then 320k), there are 8 weeks for the unrest to fade, courts have suspended at least one minors' curfew, and a curfew near the Champs-Élysées celebrations would be awkward. Market check: no Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi market for NYE was found. A Polymarket market titled 'Paris curfew announced by...?' (about $384k volume) has already resolved on the October curfews and does not apply here.
calls.dossier:
- Protests began late Sept 2026 with high-school blockades and were later joined by universities, framed around cost of living and school reform. Oct 17: over 500k marched nationwide, with evening looting at République and Les Halles and burned cars in the 10th arrondissement (samanthatravels timeline, Nov 2026).
- Oct 19: at PM Lecornu's request, the Préfecture de Police imposed a 23:00-06:00 curfew around Place de la République and Châtelet-Les Halles, 'for as long as necessary' (WaPo/ABC, Oct 20-21, 2026). Lyon and Nice imposed 21:00 curfews.
- Oct 26: the government announced school reforms and the curfew was narrowed to République only. Around Oct 28-30 a court suspended a minors' curfew. The Préfecture then issued a new 21:00-06:00 curfew for unaccompanied under-18s in several zones (including the Champs-Élysées), covering Oct 30 to Nov 2. The 23:00 curfew at République/Les Halles was reinstated for Oct 31-Nov 1, the Halloween weekend (sortiraparis; economiematin).
- All curfews ended at 06:00 on Nov 2, 2026. As of early Nov there is no curfew in Paris. The Préfecture is still issuing zone bans on gatherings (Nov 3) and RATP closed 25 metro stations for the Nov 5 general strike/protest day (sortiraparis).
- National Saturday turnout: 550k (Oct 17), 410k (Oct 24), 320k (Oct 31). A gendarme was hit by a Molotov cocktail on Oct 31.
- Pattern: the Préfecture has brought curfews back for specific high-risk nights (Halloween weekend), and courts have challenged at least one curfew.
- Historical: Paris NYE has had no curfew except the COVID-era national curfew of 2020. Usual NYE measures are fireworks, fuel and alcohol bans. NYE 2025 saw car burnings in the suburbs. After the 2005 and 2023 riots, curfews were local and lapsed within weeks.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off Préfecture de Police arrêtés (or credible reporting) of a curfew in any part of the City of Paris. A minors-only curfew in some zones would plausibly count. Gathering bans or sales bans are not curfews.
- Event window: 23:00 Dec 31, 2026 to 06:00 Jan 1, 2027 local time. As of Nov 5, 2026 the window has not started (0% elapsed), about 8 weeks away.
- Searched without finding: any announced NYE 2026 security plan, any December protest calendar, any human market on an NYE curfew (one Polymarket curfew market exists but resolved in October on the initial announcement).
calls.reference_class: Paris New Year's Eves since 2000 (curfew only in COVID-2020), adjusted for French periods of unrest where curfews were imposed (2005 banlieue riots, 2023 Nahel riots: curfews lapsed within weeks)

calls.reasoning: Status quo: no curfew in Paris since 06:00 Nov 2, 2026, and outside COVID there has been essentially no Paris New Year's Eve curfew (none after the 2005, 2023 or 2025 unrest). Upward: in Oct 2026 the Préfecture showed it will issue short curfews for specific risky nights (Halloween weekend) and minors-only curfews, New Year's Eve is a known flashpoint, and 'any part' of Paris counts. Downward: turnout fell about 40% from the peak, the government made concessions, courts have pushed back on minors' curfews, school holidays from about Dec 19 should demobilize a student-led movement, and a curfew would clash with the Champs-Élysées celebrations. Net: P(significant unrest in late Dec) about 0.25 x P(curfew | unrest) about 0.45, plus a small residual if things are calm.
calls.reconciliation: No factual disputes: all three dossiers agree that the curfews ended Nov 2, that the Préfecture reinstated a curfew for the Halloween weekend, that a court suspended a minors' curfew on Oct 28, that turnout fell, that there is no historical Paris New Year's Eve curfew outside COVID, and that no matching human market exists. The only difference is how to weigh the Préfecture's readiness to issue curfews against eight weeks of de-escalation. I added the school-holiday demobilization of a student-led movement and the conflict with the New Year's Eve celebrations, which puts me slightly below the runs. No web access on this run.

disagreements.claim: How much weight the event-targeted curfew template gets versus ongoing de-escalation over 8 weeks
disagreements.verdict: Took a slightly lower reading (0.14) because of the school holidays and the conflict with the New Year's Eve celebrations
All runs read 'any part' / 'a curfew' as including it; I agree

calls.reference_class: Paris New Year's Eves following a major autumn unrest episode (2005, 2023) plus non-COVID New Year's Eves generally
